ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) consolidated list, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's own list of designated persons. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) from foreign jurisdictions, including verification of source of wealth and funds. Continuous monitoring is mandated for the duration of the business relationship, with immediate reporting of any matches to the FIU under the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information. The screening must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Commercial Registration System (KCRS) via the Supreme Court of Korea's Registry Office (i-RO)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Hangul (Korean script). Foreign names may be transliterated phonetically. The name must include a corporate identifier such as 'Chusik Hoesa' (주식회사) or its abbreviation 'Co., Ltd.' in Korean. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. The four-tier naming convention: (1) corporate identifier, (2) trade name, (3) business purpose, (4) location (optional).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registry Office within 14 days of rejection. The appeal must be in writing, stating the grounds for reconsideration. The Registry Office must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. The applicant may also submit a new name application with modifications.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible for registration purposes under the Commercial Act, but may be rejected by the National Tax Office (NTS) for VAT registration and by financial institutions for bank account opening due to lack of physical substance. For an online luxury resale business, a physical office is recommended to satisfy substance requirements and to mitigate AML/CFT risks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered office must be a physical address in Korea; (2) Business records must be maintained at the office; (3) NTS may conduct unannounced inspections for VAT compliance; (4) Financial institutions may conduct on-site visits for AML due diligence. Quantified risk: Medium (30-50% likelihood within the first year of operation).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address (virtual) for first year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act (Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289, 292, 295, 300, 302, 316, 317 and 393; Commercial Registration Act; Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce; Personal Information Protection Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filings through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration (commercial registration application) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and paid-in capital proof
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Commercial Act, a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) has no statutory minimum paid-in capital. At least one share must be issued, and paid-in capital equals the aggregate par value of the subscribed shares. The total subscription price must be fully deposited with a commercial bank in the Republic of Korea before filing the incorporation registration, and a bank certificate of deposit must be attached. There is no legally mandated blocked escrow account for domestic paid-in capital. A non-resident shareholder must report the investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and furnish the foreign-investment report receipt to the bank; the deposited funds remain usable only after registration and bank account activation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online registration and filing portal: NTS HomeTax (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa in Korea: (1) complete Korean incorporation with the Commercial Registration Court and obtain the corporate registration certificate; (2) prepare an apostilled/certified copy of the foreign parent articles or certificate, board resolution appointing a local tax representative if no domestic place of business exists, power of attorney, lease agreement for the domestic business address, and identity documents of the representative; (3) submit the Business Registration Application, including the VAT registration block, to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the principal place of business, or through the NTS HomeTax portal; (4) obtain the 10-digit registered business number (corporate TIN) which simultaneously operates as the VAT registration number; (5) register all bank and escrow settlement accounts in the HomeTax profile; (6) appoint a Korean tax representative for VAT and electronic tax invoice matters where no permanent establishment is otherwise recognized.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic resident corporation for Korean corporate tax and VAT purposes; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Korean tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover registration threshold applies to a Chusik Hoesa: any legal entity engaging in taxable business activity in Korea must register for VAT regardless of sales amount. For sole proprietors only, an annual turnover under KRW 80,000,000 may qualify for simplified VAT taxpayer treatment; this status is not available to a Chusik Hoesa stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered corporations must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system or an NTS-certified ASP/API integration for every taxable supply of goods or services; the electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the issuance date. The NTS assigns an electronic tax invoice number to prevent duplication and reuse, and the data is automatically matched to the VAT return computation. Failure to issue or transmit an electronic tax invoice is treated as non-compliance with penalty surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero-rated export supply applies to used and vintage luxury goods sold by the Korean Chusik Hoesa to foreign buyers when the goods are physically delivered or transported out of South Korea under Korea Customs Service export clearance, title and risk pass to the foreign purchaser, and settlement is received in convertible foreign currency. Zero-rating is also available when goods are supplied through overseas consignment warehouses, provided the export declaration is executed by the Korean seller and actual export occurs within the statutory period. For online escrow sales, escrow release to the Korean entity must be supported by foreign-currency inbound remittance evidence, not domestic Won settlement alone.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) generated through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing Korean port of loading and foreign destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and consignment/escrow transaction report
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC/FIRC) or bank statement of covered receipt in foreign currency
Foreign buyer identity and order documentation for vintage luxury resale, including brand authentication report and payment authorization
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may re-characterize the supply as domestic-rated if the export documentation bundle, foreign exchange receipt, and escrow settlement trail are incomplete. The taxpayer will be assessed 10% VAT on the supply value plus additional tax, generally 10% of unpaid VAT for non-payment or late reporting, and up to 20%-40% under penalty provisions for negligent or fraudulent underreporting in serious cases, with interest for late payment. Retrospective clawback of input VAT and criminal referral may follow for fraudulent zero-rating claims, and foreign exchange repatriation beyond 180 days without an approved extension triggers additional customs and foreign exchange penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); foreign exchange supervision is administratively delegated by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and operated through licensed foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a split and asymmetric convertibility framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions, including payments for cross-border trade in vintage luxury goods, consignment fees, freight, insurance and after-sales service, are generally treated as free transactions, but must be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and are subject to factual reporting through the bank's foreign exchange information system. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity subscriptions into a Chusik Hoesa, shareholder loans and outbound portfolio investments, are not fully free; they require prior report, post-report, or certificate-based validation depending on the economic substance and size. The Korean won is not a fully internationally clearable currency; offshore onshore transfer arrangements are restricted, and any non-resident won account or offshore won repositioning must be justified and reported. Profit remittance to a foreign shareholder is permissible after the audited financial statements are approved at the shareholders' meeting and corporate income tax and dividend withholding obligations are settled. A non-resident shareholder is subject to dividend withholding at up to 22% unless a lower rate is proven under the relevant tax treaty; post-withholding remittance is normally accepted without a further FX licence. There is no mandatory cession of export proceeds to the central bank, but foreign currency receipts must be collected and repatriated to an account in Korea through a designated foreign exchange bank. The practical obstacle to convertibility is not an absolute prohibition but the documentary burden, valuation reconciliation, and the strict enforcement of anti-money-laundering and trade-data matching requirements. Therefore, real-time treasury planning must embed reporting, purpose-code discipline, and physical documentary handling rather than assume frictionless online convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 14 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds for goods shipped from Korea, including vintage luxury items sold online to overseas customers, must be received and repatriated in a recognized form to a domestic foreign exchange bank within 18 months from the date of export declaration. If the underlying trade contract stipulates a longer credit period, the exporter may apply for an exceptional extension before expiry. There is currently no mandatory surrender ratio: an exporter may retain up to 100% of receipts in a foreign-currency account at a licensed bank, or convert the proceeds into Korean won at the going market rate. The statutory surrender ratio is therefore effectively zero percent, while the repatriation and deposit obligation is absolute. Any sale of received foreign currency must be handled through a licensed foreign exchange business operator, and the conversion must be reported in the bank's surveillance system. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window can result in administrative fines, customs penalty reports, and audit flags under the Foreign Trade Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI viability is very low to non-viable. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only foreign exchange business operators approved or licensed by the Korean authorities can provide accounts and payment-clearing services to a resident entity. A Chusik Hoesa cannot lawfully open an operating account with an unlicensed offshore EMI, and using such an EMI for treasury settlement would breach Korean foreign exchange law and create a serious AML defect. Offshore EMIs may only be used as front-end payment card acquirers or website checkout connectors if the ultimate settlement flows through a licensed tier-1 Korean bank. They cannot serve as the corporate liquidity rail, capital escrow holder, or trade settlement bank. Therefore the treasury blueprint must place all primary cash management, FX clearance, and escrow functions with a top-tier domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch KYC interview is effectively mandatory for at least one statutory director or the approved local representative during initial corporate onboarding. Remote opening by consular proxy is not a full substitute: a non-resident director may be verified through an apostilled notarized power of attorney and certified passport, but a resident signatory or local compliance officer must still appear in person. For a medium-risk enhanced account such as a vintage luxury resale entity, the bank's compliance committee will normally require the Korean managing director or a named authorized officer to attend an in-person meeting, present the original corporate seal certificate, and answer questions regarding the consignment model, counterparty base and source of inventory. Video-KYC can supplement the interview for foreign shareholders but cannot replace the in-branch verification of the ultimate signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain includes individuals resident in high-risk or opaque jurisdictions without documented source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full corporate ownership chart, registry extracts from every intermediate holding jurisdiction, certified copies of passports, apostilled proof of residence, locally audited financial statements for each legal entity in the chain, personal bank statements covering at least 12 months, private wealth source documents, tax return transcripts, and independent sanctions and politically-exposed-person clearances from a recognized screening provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder does not match the corporate minimum capital file and appears to be structured to bypass foreign investment reporting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a board resolution approving the share subscription, a detailed capital call notice, the bank's foreign exchange reporting receipt, proof of the remitter's identity, original payment institution SWIFT confirmation, converted foreign currency receipt confirmation from the Korean dealing bank, and a certificate of foreign investment or post-report filing issued by the bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act once the capital has flowed into the designated escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag caused by mismatches between the luxury item invoice amount, shipping route, customs declaration, and the final online resale price paid by end consumers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble an item-level provenance dossier containing commercial invoices from upstream European and Japanese consignors, independent luxury authentication certificates, customs import declarations with valuation slips, carrier waybills and warehouse receipts, payment gateway settlement logs, refund records, and a monthly reconciliation file proving that each inbound inventory purchase corresponds to a verifiable final sale to a genuine customer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border outbound profit remittance to a non-resident shareholder without audited retained earnings availability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Korean auditor's signed financial statements, corporate income tax returns and tax payment receipts, the shareholder meeting minutes approving the dividend distribution, the dividend withholding payment receipt issued by the local tax office, supporting foreign tax authority residence certificate for treaty relief, and a board resolution confirming that no creditor objections exist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed through a designated domestic foreign exchange bank using an international SWIFT MT103 or equivalent wire, with the remitter bank exactly matching the foreign shareholder name. The purpose code must reflect an equity contribution to the Korean entity, and the beneficiary account should be a temporary capital escrow account established specifically for the injection. After receipt, the bank verifies the amount and issues a foreign capital receipt; the company then completes the post-report or prior-report process under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Capital verification is evidenced by the bank's currency exchange confirmation, a certificate of foreign investment or capital registration report, and board minutes recording the share issuance. No crypto, third-party intercompany offset or cash-surrender mechanism is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for vintage luxury inventory procurement, consignment settlement, and operational expenses must be made exclusively from a licensed bank. For standard low-value vendor payments, a SWIFT MT103 with precise remittance information, invoice reference, country of destination, and the applicable foreign exchange reporting purpose code is the primary clearing rail. For high-value procurements from European or Japanese wholesalers, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600 is preferred, supported by signed commercial invoice, authenticity certificate, packing list, and transport documents. Documentary collections at sight or with tenor are acceptable only for established counterparties with proven trade history. Escrow services embedded in the bank's liquidity platform should be used for client funds collected from online consumers; escrow release must be tied to physical inspection, authentication, and courier hand-off confirmation to reduce chargeback and structured settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts for genuine import procurement and export receivables, limited to the amount of the underlying shipment and supported by a sale or purchase contract and proforma invoice

Non-deliverable forwards only with a licensed Korean bank or through its offshore branch when the counterparty is a non-resident and the exposure is documented; speculative NDF trading by a domestic entity is not permitted

Cross-currency swaps confined to real foreign-currency debt and interest-service obligations, supported by the loan agreement and interest schedule, with no stand-alone speculative transformation of Korean won liquidity

Spot foreign exchange transactions allowed for legitimate current-account trade flows, with mandatory bank reporting and no conversion aggregation that would imply artificial structuring to evade capital account supervision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record maintained by the Chusik Hoesa; no filing to a government authority under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year end, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene may trigger a court order to convene upon shareholder petition; directors may incur a summary administrative fine not exceeding KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700). Administrative strike-off is not applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, including financial statements and tax adjustment schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty: 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; negligent under-reporting: 10%; fraudulent under-reporting: 40%; overdue daily interest surcharge: 0.022% per day. Persistent tax evasion can result in NTS asset seizure and cancellation of business registration after statutory demand and notice; Korean law does not use a company registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax (Local Income Tax surcharge on corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) via one-stop filing with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate tax return; for a 31 December fiscal year end, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local surcharge penalties mirror national corporate tax penalties: 20% for failure to file, 10% for under-reporting, 40% for fraudulent reporting, plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; prolonged delinquency may lead to local tax seizure and business deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (1 January-30 June): file by 25 July. Second half (1 July-31 December): file by 25 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional VAT tax of 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing; 10% for omitted or under-reported amounts; 40% for fraudulent tax invoices; daily late-payment interest 0.022%; continuous non-filing can trigger NTS business registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Status Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year end, by 15 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may expose the foreign-invested Korean company to an administrative fine under FIPA and may jeopardize eligibility for foreign-investment incentives; no registry strike-off, but the regulator may issue a compliance order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and audited financial statements (only when mandatory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART for public-interest and listed companies; Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) for auditor regulatory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the annual corporate tax return deadline (within three months after fiscal year end; 31 March for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-engagement of an auditor: FSS corrective order and statutory appointment; failure to file audited financial statements: administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; false audit reports: imprisonment or criminal fines up to KRW 500,000,000 (approx. USD 370,000).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No annual corporate statement of information, franchise tax, or commercial register renewal is required in South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Supreme Court Company Registration Office (Court Registry) is event-driven only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not applicable; registrations are made only for changes such as director appointment, capital increase, or dissolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No annual renewal exists, so no non-renewal penalty. If a Chusik Hoesa ceases business for at least five years, the court may, upon interested-party application, issue a judicial dissolution order, the closest Korean-equivalent administrative forfeiture.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate (progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% KRW 200M–20B; 21% KRW 20B–300B; 24% over KRW 300B, plus 10% local income tax surcharge making combined top effective rate 26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprise incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, including a 5-year corporate income tax holiday and 50% reduction for qualifying high-tech foreign investments in Free Economic Zones; R&D expense tax credits up to 30% of qualifying expenditures; deduction for technology transfer income from patents and know-how supplied to resident enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Standard and Taxable Income Computation) filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax system (beit.pe.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; intermediate semi-annual prepayments required for corporations with a business year exceeding six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year pursuant to Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act; a permitted one-month extension is available upon NTS approval, and foreign-invested companies with statutory audits may obtain an additional 1-month extension in limited circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate registration ID, business name, legal form (Chusik Hoesa), registered address, and schedule of shareholders including foreign investor details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact corporate entity code and mark any non-resident shareholder with a foreign tax residence obtained from its Tax Residency Certificate; attach the Schedule of Foreign Stockholders to validate ownership for treaty claims. Failure to declare foreign shareholders may trigger penalties for the omission of material facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales from online vintage luxury consignment, net commissions, and any other business receipts; deduct exempt income components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Korean corporation is taxed on worldwide income. For cross-border digital resale, ensure platform revenue is allocated to the Korean entity if the contracting seller is the Korean Chusik Hoesa; classify revenue from non-resident buyers as exported services only if title passes overseas and contractual and operational substance supports foreign sale; misallocation invites transfer pricing assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border transactions with non-resident related parties, including amounts of purchase, commissions, royalties, loans, and escrow fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the mandatory arm's-length pricing method selected in the transfer pricing documentation; state transaction amounts in KRW; upload the simplified TP disclosure (Form 52th) when intercompany volume exceeds KRW 3 billion and full Local/Master File when revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and intercompany volume exceeds KRW 10 billion; NTS may reject undocumented transfer prices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 23 (Foreign Tax Credit & DTA Relief Claim)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for credit or deduction of foreign income taxes and request for application of any Double Tax Agreement (DTA) reduction/exemption on dividends, interest, or royalties received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foreign tax credit computation and the completed 'Application for Tax Reduction/Exemption under Tax Treaty' for each non-resident recipient; obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued within the last six months, prove beneficial ownership, and declare that the non-resident shareholder meets the treaty's 12-month minimum holding period for reduced dividend rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the ultimate beneficial owners of the Chusik Hoesa and the substantive business location of key management and sales functions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, list the natural person ultimate beneficiary and source of wealth for funds invested; if the shareholder is a pass-through vehicle in a zero-tax jurisdiction, NTS will deny treaty relief; provide employment contracts, physical office leases, board meeting minutes, and buyer-acquisition evidence to show that core value-creating activities (marketing, authentication, pricing, and client management) are carried out in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline : additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax (or 0.03% per day of overdue amount for long delays); if no tax is due, a fixed penalty of KRW 200,000–500,000. Negligent underreporting of taxable income adds 10% of the understated tax, while intentional underreporting or false documents add 40%. Criminal prosecutions under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act carry imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 50 million for standard evasion and up to 10 years imprisonment or fines up to KRW 100 million for aggravated evasion involving foreign financial assets exceeding KRW 500 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding of 20% on dividend distributions to non-residents plus a 2% local income tax surcharge, yielding an aggregate 22% withholding tax on outbound dividends (Corporate Tax Act Article 93 and Local Income Tax Act Article 103).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Korean remitting entity must submit Form 'Application for Tax Reduction/Exemption under Tax Treaty' through NTS HomeTax before the payment date, attaching: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign jurisdiction within 6 months, (2) a shareholder listing evidencing the treaty ownership thresholds, (3) a beneficial ownership certificate confirming the recipient is not an intermediary or conduit, and (4) the audited profit allocation calculation. NTS approval may take 4–8 weeks; treaty rates typically reduce dividends to 5–15% for substantial shareholders and 10–15% for portfolio shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 20% plus 2% local surcharge (22% total), interest 20% plus 2% local surcharge (22% total). Under the Korea–US DTA, royalties are limited to 10% and interest to 10%; many other treaties provide 0% for interest and 10% for royalties; a 'limitation on benefits' clause must be satisfied by the non-resident recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File must be prepared and filed if annual revenue is at least KRW 100 billion AND cross-border related-party transaction value is at least KRW 10 billion; a simplified transfer pricing report (per Korea's Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 11) is required when the total cross-border related-party transaction amount is KRW 3 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply an OECD-style ESR/CIGA regime applicable to zero-tax jurisdictions, but economic substance is assessed through the general anti-abuse rule and controlled foreign company provisions. For an online luxury resale business, substance is evidenced by rigorous physical authentication centers in Korea, local buyer and seller contracts governed by Korean law, actual decision-making of valuation specialists in Korea, and management of the Escrow Pay settlement bank accounts in Korea; absence of such substance triggers treaty denial and CFC taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating online consignment commission revenues, fabricating vintage luxury item purchase costs through fake consignments, or concealing the Korean entity's beneficial interest in foreign Stripe and Escrow Pay accounts linked to overseas luxury auctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 10(3) of the Tax Evasion Punishment Act: imprisonment up to 10 years or fines up to KRW 100 million, plus NTS penalty of 40% of fraudulently evaded tax and daily interest of 0.03% on the unpaid amount; additionally, the proceeds of the evasion are subject to compulsory collection and asset seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under Civil Act Article 750 for tortious damages jointly with the company, including restitution of the evaded amount; NTS imposes travel bans (blacklisting) and freezing of domestic and foreign bank accounts; criminal conviction of a directing officer under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act can result in imprisonment up to 10 years, and the director's personal assets are subject to compensatory civil execution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing intercompany authentication, distribution, or escrow collection services to a Hong Kong or Singapore affiliate below arm's length to shift Korean vintage luxury resale profit outbound; failing to prepare contemporaneous Master/Local File; falsely characterizing an economically substantive Korean entity as a low-risk fixed-risk distributor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 5 and 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, NTS may re-determine taxable income at arm's length and impose additional tax equal to 5% of the adjusted income; failure to submit TP documentation gives a penalty of up to 10% of the transaction amount or an additional 30% of the underreported income, plus interest surcharges at the statutory rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved or signed false TP documentation can be held personally liable under Commercial Act Article 399 for losses sustained by the company from NTS penalties, including disgorgement of personal bonuses; criminal referral for submission of false reports to a government agency may lead to imprisonment up to 3 years and travel restrictions while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-value vintage luxury consignment payments (Stripe, Escrow Pay) without customer identification, without enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs), failing to file Cash Transaction Reports (CTRs) for transactions above KRW 10 million, or intentionally permitting an anonymous non-resident seller to launder proceeds via the consignment escrow system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information carry criminal fines up to KRW 20 million for natural persons and business sanctions including revocation of the payment affiliate registration; for serious violations, the Financial Intelligence Unit may order suspension of the entity's currency exchange or escrow licenses and impose additional administrative fines up to KRW 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were complicit in AML failures face imprisonment up to 3 years under the Act; the company's separate legal personality is pierced for money laundering predicates, and directors' personal assets can be seized for laundering proceeds; directors are subject to cross-border travel bans, addition to the Financial Supervisory Service's blacklist, and disqualification from serving as directors in any financial or e-commerce company.
